# Overview
This Quarto document provides a workflow for downloading DynLib SQL
databases from Zenodo using the `RDynLib` package, and storing them locally for subsequent use.

This workflow is a preparatory step for the subsequent DynLib workflows
and only needs to be executed when downloading a database for the first
time or retrieving a new database release.

Once downloaded, the databases can be accessed directly from their local
file paths.

The DynLib databases are publicly available on Zenodo. Each Zenodo
release may contain multiple SQLite database files, corresponding to
different analytical platforms (e.g. FTMS and QTOF) and ionization modes
(positive and negative).

# Load required R packages

```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: "hide"
#| warning: false
#| 
library(devtools)
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
library(here)
library(RDynLib)
# TODO: Replace with library(RDynLib) once the package is finalized.
load_all()
```

# Download a DynLib database from Zenodo

The `get_dynlib_zenodo()` function from the `RDynLib` package allows
DynLib databases to be downloaded directly from Zenodo.

The following arguments must be specified:

- `doi`: the Zenodo DOI of the database release.
- `file`: the name of the SQLite database file to download.
- `destdir`: the local directory in which the database will be stored.

Select the desired database from the list provided in the overview
and adapt the DOI and filename in the example below.

```{r}
# Specify the database to download
doi <- "TODO"
filename <- "maize_ftneg.sqlite"

# Specify the local destination directory
destdir <- here("data")

# Download the database
get_dynlib_zenodo(
  doi = doi,
  file = filename,
  destdir = destdir
)
```

# Verify the downloaded database

```{r}
# Local path of the downloaded database
db_path <- file.path(destdir, filename)

# Check whether the database file exists
file.exists(db_path)

# Display the local database path
db_path
```


# Next steps

The downloaded databases are now available locally and can be used
in subsequent DynLib workflows. These workflows demonstrate how to
access, query and manipulate the databases using SQL, `CompoundDb`,
`Spectra` and `RDynLib` functionalities.
